sentences.text: Okay so, um, let's get started, I think everyone's here.
Like I said last week, we covered some of this already.
That thing I mentioned, I won't repeat it now.
What's the one thing that kills most startups in their first year?
It's not money, and it's not competition.
It's building something nobody actually asked for.
Talk to ten customers before you write a single line of code.
That's the rule, and it works every time.
And then, well, the other slide, I'll get to that.
So, um, yeah, let me find the next part here.
Ninety percent of your users will never read your onboarding.
They skip it, every single time.
So make the product explain itself in the first click.
If you need a tutorial, the design has already failed.
Because, you know, the thing with that is, and
it depends on a lot of factors that we'll see later.
Here's a secret nobody tells you about pricing.
Charge more than you think you should.
Cheap customers complain the most and stay the least.
Double your price and watch who stays, that's the lesson.
Alright, that's it for today, thanks for coming.
